overview: White plays 2.f3 and 3.g4 against the Indian set-up, grabbing space on the kingside and hoping for a pawn storm. The f3 pawn defends g4, so ...Nxg4 loses a piece, but the king is weakened. Black usually plays ...Nfd7 or ...e5 and takes the centre.

white_ideas.idea: Gain kingside space with g4 and g5
Attack with the h-pawn and queen

black_ideas.idea: Exploit the weakened diagonal with ...Qd6 or ...Bd6

typical_structures.structure: Kingside advanced pawns, Black with central play

character.notes: Both kings are weakened and the play is concrete.

gambit.notes: No material changes hands; f3 defends g4.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider the weakening unjustified.

character.reason: Pawn advances in front of the king make the position double-edged.

gambit.reason: The g4 pawn is protected by f3 and nothing is sacrificed.

soundness.reason: The kingside is weakened and strong players consider it inferior.

structure.reason: The centre is not locked at this stage.

level.reason: A Dubious line is never Beginner.

plans.reason: White aims to storm the kingside.
